objective_for_doctor: Evaluate and manage a patient presenting with left chest pain, a productive cough with purulent sputum, and shortness of breath.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

“About a week ago I started having left-sided chest pain along with a productive cough with purulent sputum, and I’ve also felt short of breath. I had flu recently but didn’t follow the treatment plan, and I’ve had fever and malaise since then.”
Does the chest pain worsen when you take a deep breath or cough, or does it feel more like a constant pressure or squeezing sensation?
“It definitely gets worse when I cough and with deep breaths, and it feels more sharp than like a constant pressure or squeezing. I’m also feeling quite uncomfortable with the shortness of breath.”
What is the highest temperature you have recorded since these symptoms began?
“I measured my highest temperature around 102°F (about 38.9°C) since this started.”
Have you experienced any shaking chills or rigors along with the fever?
“Yes, I’ve had shaking chills with the fever—like rigors at times—especially in the first few days. I’ve felt pretty weak and miserable overall.”
“My sputum is yellow to green, and it looks pretty purulent. It’s been coming up with the cough most days for the past week.”
Do you have a history of smoking or any chronic lung conditions like asthma or COPD?
“No, I don’t smoke, and I don’t have asthma or COPD or any chronic lung condition. I’ve otherwise been pretty healthy before this happened.”
